content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], I read your post because I experienced similar issues installing [product_name] V8 on my Debian 64-bit computer (Debian Bullseye). After following the setup instructions for running this software on Linux, everything appears to work: I can launch [product_name] and design networks. However, when attempting to use networking functions, I receive a Java error stating "adapter type is not support." I am able to ping the device connected to the Ethernet port, so connectivity itself is not the problem. Running [product_name] V8 on Windows 10 works smoothly, with no errors. I'm out of solutions at this point. Does anyone have suggestions? Kind regards, [user_name]
Hi [user_name], Are you using the latest version of [product_name] (V8.3)? "Download for [product_name] 8.3 Software Upgrade" [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report encountering a Java error message ("adapter type is not support") when attempting to use networking features in [product_name] V8 on Debian Bullseye (64-bit Linux). While the software launches and allows network design, network communication fails exclusively under Linux. The same software works correctly on Windows 10, indicating an operating system-specific issue with networking support.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] V8 to provide seamless network functionality on Debian Bullseye (Linux 64-bit) comparable to its performance on Windows 10, without adapter compatibility errors.
